# Hardcover -> Obsidian

For n8n 2.44.6 and Obsidian Local REST API 5.5.2. Imported INACTIVE and PREVIEW ONLY.
Daily at 04:30 Europe/Madrid, plus manual runs. One-way; Hardcover is never modified.

## Credentials
Create Bearer Auth "Hardcover read-only": enter only your API token, without the Bearer prefix.
Create it at https://hardcover.app/account/api with read:me:content, read:library, read:catalog:data.
Do not grant write/all permissions, double-prefix Bearer, or put secrets in Settings/notes.
Assign it to Read Hardcover identity, Read Hardcover page, and Resolve ISBN and ASIN.
Use Bearer Auth "Obsidian Local REST API": enter only your VM API key, without the Bearer prefix.
Assign it to all Obsidian HTTP nodes. Use the existing trusted HTTPS proxy hostname, not localhost.

## First run
1. Confirm Settings point to the correct VM/vault and _templates/book.md exists there.
2. Execute the WHOLE workflow from Manual preview with previewOnly=true.
3. Inspect Preview or unchanged: creates, updates, not-in-library notes and conflicts.
4. Resolve identity conflicts by setting the correct numeric hardcover_id in the existing note external-sync comment.
5. Keep a vault/Seafile backup before the first write. This workflow does not create backup ZIPs.
6. Set previewOnly=false, run manually, inspect Verify persisted books and resulting notes.
7. Only then publish/activate the daily schedule. Both triggers use the same Settings.

## Scope and matching
Reads your entire authenticated library, including all six statuses, using ID-cursor pagination.
Pages continue until empty (not until shorter than 100), so server-side row caps do not truncate the library.
Searches all Markdown notes recursively under databases/books via the native REST JsonLogic endpoint.
The API glob operator uses folder/*.md for direct and nested notes; folder/**/*.md skips direct children.
Matches hardcover_id first, then edition ISBN/ASIN, then normalized title AND author names.
Name-token comparison tolerates existing family-name-first author spelling.
Potential alternate editions/titles, multiple IDs, duplicates and filename collisions block ALL writes.
A preview lists conflicts; a write run throws before any PUT if a conflict remains.
No fuzzy auto-merges, no deletions, and no automatic renames of existing notes.
Bind hardcover_id in the hidden external-sync comment when a translation, abridgement or catalog merge is ambiguous.
New notes use Authors - Title.md when authors are known; trailing English articles are moved to the front.
Books without primary authors are still created as Title.md, with author: [] and a visible warning.
They retain hardcover_id, so later runs fill empty author metadata without creating duplicate notes.
Editors/illustrators are not relabeled as authors. Unknown metadata stays null/empty.
Later author enrichment does not rename the existing file or rewrite its body/headings.
Unsafe filename characters become separators; long/colliding names require a manually named bound note.
Set createMissingNotes=false to update matching existing notes without creating the rest of the library.

## Fields and ownership
Hardcover controls status, rating, started and finished in frontmatter.
A deleted/unset rating or date on Hardcover clears that managed property, including on the first sync.
Rating is YOUR rating on a 0-5 scale, not the community average.
Statuses map 1->Not Read, 2->In Progress, 3->Read, 4->Paused, 5->Did Not Finish, 6->Ignored.
Dates use the latest read-through by record ID. An unfinished reread never inherits a previous finish.
If no read-through exists, use first_started_reading_date and last_read_date when supplied.
Finished-date precision is retained in the sync comment; partial/year-only dates are not asserted to be exact.
Existing created is unchanged; new notes use today in Europe/Madrid.
Technical hardcover_* and kindle-* metadata lives in a hidden external-sync HTML comment, never in frontmatter.
The comment contains JSON: {"version":1,"properties":{"hardcover_id":123}} between <!-- external-sync and --> lines.
Library-added dates, source IDs/URLs, edition bindings, alternate IDs and Kindle import provenance are retained there.
Legacy frontmatter is read and relocated when a matched note is updated; conflicting or malformed state stops writes.
Preserve the comment when moving or backing up a note. Third-party importers must support this format before resuming.
Fill empty author/title/source/ISBN/ASIN/category only; preserve populated bibliographic fields.
Existing Amazon source links remain; the Hardcover link is retained as hardcover_url in the hidden comment.
ISBN/ASIN are only filled from a matching edition, not an arbitrary edition of the same book.
Invalid optional catalog ISBNs/ASINs are ignored, with book/edition/field/value warnings in issues.
A valid ISBN-10 remains usable when ISBN-13 is bad, and vice versa. No checksum is guessed or repaired.
These catalog warnings do not stop unrelated books or disable identity/concurrency safeguards.
Category uses only Hardcover literary_type_id: Fiction or Nonfiction. Topics are never guessed.
New notes inherit the book template, including its body and other properties.
Supported tokens: date:YYYY-MM-DD, VALUE:book_author(s), VALUE:book_title, VALUE:main_topic (blank).
Unsupported Templater/dynamic tokens stop creation; none are left silently unresolved.

## Preservation and failures
Existing handwriting, highlights, block IDs and unrelated YAML are preserved; technical metadata moves to the sync comment.
Raw managed YAML is checked against the REST metadata cache before matching/editing.
Unsupported/ambiguous YAML, stale cache, invalid local identifiers, structural API errors or GraphQL errors fail before writes.
PUT uses If-Match for updates and If-None-Match:* for creates. Never bypass a 412.
Every successful write is read back for exact comparison. Identical data makes no further edits.
All HTTP nodes use Response Format=Autodetect with Include Response Headers and Status enabled.
Autodetect may return JSON in body or text in data, even when outputPropertyName=body is set; both are supported.
Vendor JSON text is parsed explicitly; Markdown read-back is compared verbatim, without trimming or JSON parsing.
Do not force JSON/Text response modes: an undecoded stream can freeze the n8n output viewer.
TLS checks stay enabled, redirects are disabled, and reads have bounded retries only.
Catalog lookups are paced; each looped library page waits 1.1 seconds before the next.
No automatic retries for PUT. A failed batch may already have written earlier notes: rerun the full preview.
Do not run overlapping executions. Conditional writes protect file versions, not distributed Seafile merges.
Check SFConflict files and pause competing book imports while testing.
The API is beta: GraphQL changes or missing token scopes fail explicitly.
Automatic/manual execution payload retention is disabled. Do not pin personal library data or share exports.
Workflow structure and logic can be checked offline; authenticated live execution/import needs your credentials.

## References
https://docs.hardcover.app/api/getting-started/
https://docs.hardcover.app/api/graphql/schemas/userbooks/
https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/schema.graphql
https://github.com/coddingtonbear/obsidian-local-rest-api/blob/5.5.2/docs/openapi.yaml
